definition: Vestige means a mark or trace of something lost or vanished.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word vestige. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know vestige should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The only vestige of the estate's formal gardens is a line of box hedge running straight through the parking lot.
A leftover is far milder than a vestige — plenty still remains, and it is still perfectly usable.
A remnant is weaker than a vestige — a remnant is still a real piece of the original, while a vestige is only the faintest mark that it ever existed.

A trace is the faintest sign that anything was present — a trace of smoke, of an accent, of doubt — and the thing itself may still exist nearby. A vestige is a trace with a history: the mark left by something otherwise vanished, proof that it once passed this way.

A relic is an object from the past that people deliberately keep — in a case, a shrine, a drawer — often with reverence. A vestige is not kept at all: it is the accidental mark a vanished thing left behind, a footprint rather than a possession.
